title: What is the smallest multiple of all of one to ten except seven?
description: The numbers one to ten, except seven, must all go into one number. Writing the multiples of nine, then the multiples of seventy two, leads to the smallest such number, and a check puts it back against every number.
teaching_notes: One idea: the numbers that matter are eight, nine and five, and the common multiples of a pair are the multiples of one number. Watch for students who multiply all nine numbers together.

source: Figure it Out box 2, Q9, p.111 (Try This)
video_script.why: The child builds the smallest number step by step, first a multiple of nine and eight, then a multiple of five as well.
video_script.substitution: Find the first number in two lists, then the first number in that list and a third list.
video_script.anchor: the numbers one to ten with seven crossed out, and a growing list of multiples
video_script.payoff_line: The smallest number is three hundred and sixty

final_answer.spoken: the smallest number is three hundred and sixty

maths_rules: a multiple of 8 is a multiple of 2 and 4; a multiple of 9 is a multiple of 3; 5 is needed for 5 and 10; 6 is covered by 2 and 3
multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72; the first that is also a multiple of 8 is 72
multiples of 72: 72, 144, 216, 288, 360; the first ending in 0 or 5 is 360
video_script.design: One idea: build the smallest number from the numbers that matter, using the first meeting number of two lists as the new list. Same method as the book example: common multiples are the multiples of one number.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a number that is a multiple of many numbers.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Find the smallest number that is a multiple of every number from one to ten, except seven.

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: two lists of multiples, the first number in both lists marked

marks.way: the example from the book is pointed to
marks.lists: two lists of multiples are written with a number in both marked
marks.more: a third list slides in under the other two

narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='lists'/>A number that is a multiple of two numbers sits in both their lists.
<bookmark mark='more'/>We can keep adding one more number, and the lists must still meet.

marks.given: the nine numbers are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers one to ten, except seven.

beats.on_screen: To find: the smallest number that is a multiple of all of them

marks.find: the words To find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the smallest number that is a multiple of all of them.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: a multiple of 8 is a multiple of 2 and 4; a multiple of 9 is a multiple of 3; 5 is needed for 5 and 10

marks.pick: 2 and 4 are joined to 8 by arrows
marks.nine: 3 is joined to 9 and 5 is joined to 10

narration: <bookmark mark='pick'/>Step one, pick the numbers that matter. A multiple of eight is a multiple of two and four.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>A multiple of nine is a multiple of three. Five is needed for five and ten.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72; the first that is also a multiple of 8 is 72

marks.nine: the multiples of 9 are written up to 72

narration: <bookmark mark='nine'/>Step two, write the multiples of nine: nine, eighteen, twenty seven, and on to seventy two.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>The first one that is also a multiple of eight is seventy two.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: multiples of 72: 72, 144, 216, 288, 360; the first that is also a multiple of 5 ends in 0 or 5: 360

marks.seventytwo: the multiples of 72 are written in a row
marks.five: 360 glows and the last digit 0 is marked

narration: <bookmark mark='seventytwo'/>Step three, write the multiples of seventy two: seventy two, one hundred and forty four, and on.
<bookmark mark='five'/>The one after two hundred and eighty eight is three hundred and sixty. It ends in zero, so it is a multiple of five.

marks.more: 360 = 4 x 90, 5 x 72 and 6 x 60 are written
marks.rest: 360 = 8 x 45, 9 x 40 and 10 x 36 are written and all get a tick

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step four, check them all. Three hundred and sixty is two times one hundred and eighty, and three times one hundred and twenty.
<bookmark mark='more'/>It is also four times ninety, five times seventy two, and six times sixty.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Eight times forty five, nine times forty, and ten times thirty six work too.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The smallest number is three hundred and sixty.
